questions.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}\},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ -6\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -2 \\ -6\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$,  ${x}_{2}$, and ${x}_{3}$ such that  

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2}+{x}_{3}{b}_{3} & =x \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ -6\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -2 \\ -6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

From this, we get the system with the augmented matrix $M$, which we reduce using Gaussian elimination: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 0 & 6 \\ -3 & 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & -6 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & 12 & 2 & 16 \\ 0 & -6 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & 12 & 2 & 16 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

  

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=6 \\ 12{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=16 \\ {x}_{3}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=2.$ Substituting this into the second  equation yields

$$
12{x}_{2}+2(2)=16\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=1.
$$

 Finally,  by substituting ${x}_{2}=1$ into the first equation we obtain 

$$
{x}_{1}+4(1)=6\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=2.
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

So, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=2+1+2=5.
$$

questions.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{2}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Remember, the order of the vectors in a basis is important.

Notice that 

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}={{(\,4\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{1}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{b}_{1}}+{{(\,-3\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{b}_{2}}
$$

which means that

$$
x=4\cdot {b}_{1}+(-3)\cdot {b}_{2}
$$

and therefore

$$
[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ \,\,-3\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, we have that ${x}_{2}=-3.$

questions.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 8 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{1}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Remember, the order of the vectors in a basis is important.

Notice that 

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 8 \\ 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}={{(\,3\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{1}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{b}_{1}}+{{(\,8\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{b}_{2}}
$$

which means that

$$
x=3\cdot {b}_{1}+8\cdot {b}_{2}
$$

and therefore

$$
[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 8\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, we have that ${x}_{1}=3.$

questions.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 9\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2} & =x \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The equation above gives the system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ -3 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ -3 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & -5 & 15\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=2 \\ -5{x}_{2}=15.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=-3.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}-2(-3)=2\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-4.
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -3\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(-4)+(-3)=-7.$

questions.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}\},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ -4\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -15 \\ 6\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$,  ${x}_{2}$, and ${x}_{3}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{b}_{1}+{x}_{2}{b}_{2}+{x}_{3}{b}_{3} & =x \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ -4\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -15 \\ 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

From this, we get the system with the augmented matrix $M$, which we reduce using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 7 \\ -2 & -3 & -2 & -15 \\ 4 & -2 & -4 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 & -1 \\ 4 & -2 & -4 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-4){R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & -6 & -4 & -22\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-6){R}_{2} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 8 & -16\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=7 \\ -{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=-1 \\ 8{x}_{3}=-16.\end{aligned}
$$

From third equation we get ${x}_{3}=-2$ and substituting this value into the second equation yields ${x}_{2}=-2(-2)+1=5.$ Finally, substituting ${x}_{2}=5$ into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}+5=7\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=2.
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$

Finally, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=2+5+(-2)=5.
$$
